title: Variant safeguard: sequential statistical tests, exposure ramps, and shadow launch controls
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a first-class A/B and canary experimentation framework for model versions focused on safe rollouts. This ticket covers experiment setup UX, exposure and ramp controls (time-based and event-based), sequential statistical checks (alpha spending, stopping rules), shadow traffic plumbing, and automatic rollback triggers for safety regressions. The goal is to enable product and platform engineers to run short-lived canaries, multi-armed experiments, and continuous shadow tests with strong guardrails that prevent customer-facing regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Console UI: experiment creation flow that supports canary and A/B modes, exposure schedules (linear, exponential, manual), and optional shadow-only routing
Exposure engine: server-side percent bucketing and time-based ramp policy that can be paused/modified without redeploy
Stats engine: sequential testing library integrated into the runtime that supports user-configurable alpha spending functions and minimum sample thresholds
Observability: per-variant dashboards with sample counts, latency P50/P90/P99, token-cost per request, and custom quality metrics from user-provided evals
Auto-rollback: configurable safety rules (e.g., delta_latency > 2x, increase in error rate > 0.5%, quality metric drop > 3%) that trigger automatic traffic rollback and create an incident ticket
Shadow traffic: ability to mirror X% of production traffic to a variant without affecting responses, with sampled diffs and KL/divergence style signals captured
APIs and SDKs: endpoints for creating/stopping experiments programmatically and fetching real-time exposure allocations
Audit and compliance: experiment audit trail capturing creator, changes, and exposures stored for 1 year (configurable)
notes: Design trade-off: prefer conservative default alpha spending (O'Brien-Fleming style) to minimize false positives on small canaries; allow advanced users to choose Pocock or continuous monitoring modes
We will implement sequential checks server-side to centralize decisioning and prevent client drift. This increases coupling but simplifies rollout rollbacks and audit logs.
Shadow traffic is implemented as asynchronous mirroring to avoid tail latency impact. Mirrored requests are sampled for token-level cost analysis and stored in a compressed trace store.
To reduce cost, prefix/KV cache warmup for canaries will reuse existing warm caches where possible; however, this can bias latency metrics — we will annotate warm-cache experiments explicitly.
Safety escalation: auto-rollback creates a standardized incident with stack traces and an optional revert flag for model variants in Dedicated and Private deployments

comments: Sofia Martinez (Design): Request to surface warm-cache annotation in the metric timeline — otherwise teams will misinterpret improved latencies.
Ethan Zhou (Research): Recommend defaulting to two-stage rollouts: 1% -> 10% with a 24h hold to capture rare regressions before larger exposure.
Priya Raman (SRE): Auto-rollback should integrate with existing alerting (PagerDuty) and include a dry-run mode for safety-rule evaluation without changing traffic.
Liam O'Connor (Assignee): Planning to prototype the sequential checks with live A/A runs first to calibrate false positive rates. Will share early telemetry in two weeks.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (A/A calibration): run 48h A/A on production with stats engine to tune false positive thresholds
Phase 1 (shadow launch): mirror 5% of traffic for 7 days, collect diffs and quality signals
Phase 2 (canary): linear ramp 0.5% -> 1% -> 5% with 12h holds, sequential checks at each hold
Phase 3 (scale): 10% -> 25% -> 50% after stability gates, then full promotion
Abort policy: if any safety rule triggers, rollback to previous allocation and open incident; require manual approval to restart the experiment
monitoring_signals: Correctness: user-defined quality evals (per-prompt scoring) with baseline delta and confidence intervals
Latency: p50/p90/p99 with baseline ratio and absolute ms thresholds
Errors: model runtime errors, HTTP 5xx, tokenization failures
Cost: avg token cost and tokens per request delta
Upstream regressions: KL divergence and response distribution drift in shadow diffs
rollback_rules: Immediate rollback if error rate increases by >0.5% absolute and sustained for 30 minutes
Rollback if latency p99 > baseline_p99 * 2 for 1 hour
Rollback if user-defined quality metric drops by >3% with p < 0.05 in sequential test
Soft-stop (pause ramp) if sample size for variant < configured minimum after scheduled hold
